perspective:
Available to Brandon:

- Brandon is an insurance agent. He first meets Benjamin Erickson in a professional setting, where Benjamin seeks business insurance advice. Brandon is aware Benjamin has limited formal education and is concerned about explaining complex insurance clearly. He hears Benjamin wants comprehensive coverage and is unfamiliar with some terms. Brandon explains liability insurance as a safety net, gives a slip-and-fall legal/medical costs example, and explains asset protection for inventory/equipment as guarding physical investments. He hears Benjamin say it makes sense, ask for an example, and thank him for breaking it down.
- In their next meeting, based on their prior interaction, Brandon now feels more confident Benjamin can understand details and plans to discuss more complex aspects. He hears Benjamin say he is ready and has been reading. Brandon explains business interruption insurance as covering income loss when normal operations stop, and property insurance as covering damage and theft. He hears Benjamin call this important and reassuring.
- At a casual lunch, Brandon worries he is too detail-focused and wants to keep discussions engaging. He hears Benjamin say he appreciates thoroughness but also enjoys lighter moments. Brandon tells a joke about an entrepreneur insuring his taste buds for a million dollars and relates it to assessing unique risks. He hears Benjamin find it fascinating and agree risk assessment matters.
- Pleased by Benjamin’s positive response to his anecdote, Brandon decides to add value beyond insurance. He asks whether strategic investments could lower premiums and suggests upgraded security systems protect assets and may reduce insurance costs. He hears Benjamin agree to explore this.
- Encouraged by their strong rapport and mutual benefits, Brandon proposes a joint venture: co-developing a platform integrating risk management with financial planning for entrepreneurs. He hears Benjamin agree, call it groundbreaking, say combining their expertise could set them apart, and agree to draft initial plans.
